Question Choices: What is the period of y = cos(x)? Use radians; x ranges over all real inputs where the function is defined.
Hints: Cosine repeats after one full rotation.;A full rotation is 2pi radians.
Solution: The base cos repeats after its argument increases by 2pi radians. With B=1, the least positive period is T=2pi/|B|=2*pi. Check |B|T=2*pi, one full cycle.

Question Choices: What is the period of y = tan(x)? Use radians; x ranges over all real inputs where the function is defined.
Hints: Tangent repeats twice during a full turn.;Its period is half of 2pi.
Solution: At x+pi, both sine and cosine change sign, so their quotient tan(x+pi)=tan(x) wherever defined. This is the least positive period: pi radians. The graph repeats between successive vertical asymptotes.

Question Choices: What is the range of y = sin(x)? Use radians; x ranges over all real inputs where the function is defined.
Hints: The unit-circle y-coordinate stays between -1 and 1.;Include both endpoints.
Solution: Unit-circle coordinates always lie between -1 and 1, and both endpoints are attained. Since sine and cosine read those coordinates, each has exact range [-1,1], including both ends.
